topic: How would the 0.25 dB passband loss affect link budget margins in low-noise satellite receiver frontends?
consensus_response: A 0.25 dB passband loss directly impacts receiver sensitivity, increasing interference and noise floor, degrading SNR, and reducing link budget margins. This loss directly impacts receiver noise figure, leading to increased noise floor, reduced SNR, and decreased data rates. Antenna diversity mitigates some of this impact, but it is not a complete solution.  The trade-off between power and signal quality is crucial, impacting the overall link budget.
